items.grounds: Both sides re-derived from bytes. LEFT (the preceding unit's close): the refrain clause וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא closes oshb:Isa.2.17 (byte tier) and recurs byte-identically as the close of oshb:Isa.2.11 (sweep: 2 verses at byte tier, and 2 at skeleton — the only two sites in the book); the two stanzas it closes each open on a ruled onset — the vocative-plus-imperative summons בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה at oshb:Isa.2.5 (byte tier; sweep: 1 verse skeleton) and the temporal-formula onset כִּ֣י י֞וֹם לַיהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת at oshb:Isa.2.12 (byte tier; sweep: 1 verse skeleton) — so the refrain's bracket function is argued from bytes at both sites, and under the strategy's refrain-close rule (refrains close units; a refrain that byte-recurs at the close of successive stanzas brackets each stanza) the 2:17|2:18 seam is warranted from the left by a ruled tier-1 CLOSE. RIGHT: וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף (oshb:Isa.2.18, byte tier, the whole verse) carries no ruled onset class — the finding's onset-only reading re-derives exactly — but a waw-prefixed opener is not counterevidence to a seam: the accepted onsets וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא at oshb:Isa.7.18 and וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י at oshb:Isa.11.1 (both byte tier) are waw-prefixed. Tier-3: the staged parashah inventory records SAMEKH at Isa.2.11 and PE at Isa.2.22 and no seg at Isa.2.17 or Isa.2.18 (single witness; absence weighed as nothing). The filed claim that 'the warrant is topical shift alone' therefore fails the complete test: the shipped row grounds its opening on 'the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17' and 'the refrain-closed catalogue' and cites web:Isa.2.17 and web:Isa.2.5-Isa.2.17 — the row weighed the left side; the finding did not. The prior adjudication applied the no-tier-1-at-own-seam rule from the opening verse alone and treated the refrain as context rather than as the ruled close; the both-sides law reverses that outcome. The continuity facts the finding cites do not erase the close: the four-token flight core מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר collates byte at oshb:Isa.2.10 and accent_stripped at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 1 verse byte, 3 verses accent_stripped), and the idols lexeme stands at oshb:Isa.2.8, oshb:Isa.2.18 and oshb:Isa.2.20 (אֱלִילִ֑ים, אֱלִילֵ֣י, byte tier; sweep: 8 verses skeleton book-wide, 3 in this chapter) — both motifs bind 2:18-22 to the FIRST stanza (2:5-11) across the whole of 2:12-17, so they straddle the 2:11 refrain close exactly as they straddle the 2:17 one; they argue the poem-level envelope over 2:5-22 that the neighbour row already discloses as a rival, not a merger of 2:18-22 with 2:12-17. The verse-initial temporal formula בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ at oshb:Isa.2.20 (byte tier; bare-form sweep: 45 verses skeleton) is an in-unit formula two verses past a seam already warranted from the left. Residual defect, real but low: the row engages its load-bearing left-side warrant by reference only — no oshb:Isa.2.17 in boundary_evidence_refs, no spliced refrain bytes or tier label in its own fields (the byte-tier splice lives only in the neighbour row), no refrain.* signal key in observed_substrate_signals, and its rejected-alternative sentence restates the bound as 'topical shift ... and the petuchah break', leaning on a tier-3 mark and omitting the tier-1 close — an engagement-class and field-contract gap, not a missing warrant; confidence medium is defensible, and the high-confidence aggravator that sets this class at medium elsewhere is absent. Span ruling: decline the routing proposal. Branch (a), Isa.2.12-Isa.2.22, would erase a refrain-closed boundary while leaving the byte-identical 2:11 close standing, and shows from no byte why the refrain closes a unit at 2:11 but not at 2:17; the motifs it would lean on bind 2:18-22 to 2:5-11, not to 2:12-17. Branch (b), Isa.2.20-Isa.2.22, is byte-unsound: it severs the eight-token run מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ, byte-identical at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses byte tier), and leaves 2:18-19 as a tail closing on nothing. Branch (c)'s 'tier-1 shortfall at the opening seam' does not exist under the complete test. The span Isa.2.18-Isa.2.22 stands — warranted at its front by the 2:17 refrain close and at its rear by the imperative close חִדְל֤וּ לָכֶם֙ מִן הָ֣אָדָ֔ם at oshb:Isa.2.22 (byte tier; sweep: 2 verses skeleton for the imperative) with PE corroboration and the fresh hinneh-announcement onset כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת at oshb:Isa.3.1 (byte tier). The cure is a field repair (splice and tier-label the 2:17 refrain, add oshb:Isa.2.17, add a refrain.* key, re-cut the rejected-alternative sentence so the bound is the refrain close with the PE as corroboration), and the adjacent row Isa.2.12-Isa.2.17 is ruled coherently: its refrain close stands.

One source occurrence with P02-011#1 (the shared 7:17|7:18 seam); ruled coherently with it. The proposal's 718_ext placeholder resolves to וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.7.18, tokens 1-3, byte tier; the slice's resolution string is byte-equal to the source splice) and the item is ruled with that text. Both sides re-derived. LEFT (this row's own close): oshb:Isa.7.17 closes the named-participant scene in direct second-person address — יָבִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה עָלֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל עַמְּךָ֮ וְעַל בֵּ֣ית אָבִיךָ֒ (byte tier) carries three 2ms pronominal suffixes (a suffix scan of oshb:Isa.7.17 finds exactly these three) — and the staged parashah inventory records PE at Isa.7.17 (single witness, tier-3 corroboration only). RIGHT (the following unit's onset): וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא opens oshb:Isa.7.18 verse-initially (byte tier), a formula onset of the class the neighbouring rows treat as a driver (the extended form sweeps 5 verses at byte tier and 13 at accent_stripped, oshb:Isa.7.21 and oshb:Isa.7.23 among the 13; the bare in-that-day skeleton 45 verses), and the person shifts at the seam itself from 2ms address to third-person announcement, יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier), with no 2nd-person pronominal suffix anywhere in oshb:Isa.7.18-7.25 (suffix scan: 0 hits). The seam is therefore warranted from BOTH sides by byte-true ruled signals that the row itself already splices and cites — which is why the finding and the prior adjudication agree the placement is not the defect. What the complete test changes is the weight of the defect. The row's load-bearing clause is two-part: (i) a frame-mode shift 'at MT 7:18 itself' — byte-true at the seam (three 2ms suffixes at 7:17 against none at 7:18; a narrated scene with a named addressee giving way to an unaddressed announcement); (ii) a cycle-wide generalisation that 7:18-25 'names no speaker and addresses no one directly'. 'Names no speaker' holds: the divine-speech census places no koh-amar, neum, or amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH site anywhere in oshb:Isa.7.18-7.25 (nearest: the divine frame at oshb:Isa.7.7 and the narrative onset וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י at oshb:Isa.8.1, byte tier). 'Addresses no one directly' is byte-OPEN, not byte-false: the sole candidate is תָב֣וֹא inside לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה יִרְאַ֖ת שָׁמִ֣יר וָשָׁ֑יִת (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier), a qal imperfect whose 2ms and 3fs forms are identical in the pointed bytes; no morphology layer is staged, so the parse cannot be machine-settled, and the 3fs parse — the feminine construct noun that follows as its subject, 'the fear of briers and thorns shall not come there' — is byte-available and is paralleled by יָ֣בוֹא שָׁ֑מָּה in the preceding verse (oshb:Isa.7.24, byte tier), the third-person 'one comes there'. The row's own second witness renders it second person — “you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) — while rendering the cycle's two other taw-prefixed forms, תִּסְפֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.7.20, byte tier) and תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה (oshb:Isa.7.24, byte tier), as third person; the row quotes that rendering and neither argues the parse nor reconciles it. Under the tier-disclosure standard a form-class claim is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses; as shipped the clause is unsupported and witness-contradicted, and against the facing row's 'addressed to the same audience' / 'the four share one addressee' (where 'addressee' means the oracle's target, not a grammatical addressee) the two rows are terminologically inconsistent. The prior adjudication applied the byte-false-load-bearing-warrant rule, testing the characterisation at the cycle's far end (7:25) and treating the demoted formula as if absent; on the complete test the load-bearing kernel (the shift at the seam) is byte-true, sound warrants stand on both sides in the row's own splices, and the defective part is an over-extended, unargued generalisation plus the row's inverted ordering ('cannot discriminate the cut on its own' — a first-site formula onset does discriminate: nothing of the class stands at oshb:Isa.7.17). A defective load-bearing warrant over a byte-sound, twice-warranted seam is the medium class of this queue (defective warrant, boundary uncontested), not high. Downgrade to medium. Cure as proposed, no span change: delete the 'addresses no one directly' clause, re-argue the rear seam from the 7:17 second-person close and the 7:18 formula onset with the PE as tier-3 corroboration, and align the two rows' 'addressee' wording.

One source occurrence with P02-010#1 (the shared 7:17|7:18 seam); ruled coherently with it — same both-sides derivation, same outcome. The proposal's 718_ext placeholder resolves to וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.7.18, tokens 1-3, byte tier; the slice's resolution string is byte-equal to the source splice) and the item is ruled with that text. LEFT (the preceding unit's close): יָבִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה עָלֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל עַמְּךָ֮ וְעַל בֵּ֣ית אָבִיךָ֒ (oshb:Isa.7.17, byte tier) — three 2ms pronominal suffixes closing the named-participant scene (suffix scan: exactly three), PE at Isa.7.17 in the staged parashah inventory (single witness, tier-3). RIGHT (this row's own opening verse): וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא verse-initial (byte tier; 5 verses byte, 13 accent_stripped including oshb:Isa.7.21 and oshb:Isa.7.23 — the row's own tier-labelled recurrence digits re-verify — and the bare skeleton 45 verses), followed by the third-person announcement יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ (byte tier), with 0 second-person suffixes across oshb:Isa.7.18-7.25: formula onset plus person shift at the seam verse itself. The front seam is warranted from both sides by bytes the row already splices; the placement is not the defect. The defect re-derives inside this row's own boundary_rationale, but at a lower weight than filed. The field first demotes the formula ('cannot discriminate the cut on its own'), then rests the seam on the frame-mode characterisation, then two sentences later says the cycle is 'marked off from it by their own repeated formula rather than a fresh scene' — re-asserting the formula it demoted — and calls the cycle 'addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative' while the rejected alternative adds 'the four share one addressee ... lacking any addressee shift'; read with 'addressee' as the oracle's target these are loose rather than flatly contradictory, but the field is muddled at its load-bearing point. The byte test of 'addresses no one directly' is open, not false: תָב֣וֹא in לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה יִרְאַ֖ת שָׁמִ֣יר וָשָׁ֑יִת (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier) is 2ms/3fs-ambiguous in the pointed bytes with no morphology layer staged; the 3fs parse with the following feminine construct noun as subject is byte-available and parallels יָ֣בוֹא שָׁ֑מָּה (oshb:Isa.7.24, byte tier); the row's own closing quotation renders it second person — “you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) — while the same witness renders תִּסְפֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.7.20) and תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה (oshb:Isa.7.24), the cycle's other two taw-prefixed forms, as third person; the row neither argues the parse nor reconciles its own quoted witness, so under the tier-disclosure standard the clause is unsupported and witness-contradicted as written. 'Names no speaker' holds (no koh-amar, neum, or amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH site in oshb:Isa.7.18-7.25 in the divine-speech census; the next narrative onset is וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י at oshb:Isa.8.1, byte tier). The prior adjudication applied the byte-false-load-bearing-warrant rule to the 7:25 rendering and the in-field wording; the complete test finds the seam-kernel of the row's warrant (the shift at MT 7:18 itself) byte-true and the seam twice warranted in-row, leaving an unsupported over-generalisation and muddled ordering in the load-bearing field — the defective-warrant-over-uncontested-seam class this queue rates medium. Downgrade to medium, coherently with P02-010#1. Cure as proposed, no span change: delete the 'addresses no one directly' clause, re-argue the front seam from the 7:18 formula onset taken with the 7:17 second-person close (PE as tier-3 corroboration), settle the field's own stance on the formula, and reconsider confidence (medium, frontier_flag_considered false) once restated.

Both sides re-derived; every ref here is in zone A and dual-cited. RIGHT (the row's own opening verse): כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ opens oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1) (byte tier); the particle also opens oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) inside the span, as the row itself shows, so the row disqualifies its only formal marker and rests the seam on 'the turn from darkened lands to light and glory the verse carries, not on the particle' — verified verbatim. No ruled onset class (hoy, hinneh, koh-amar, neum, massa header, imperative, vocative, addressee shift, verse-initial temporal formula) stands in that verse; the temporal-contrast pair כָּעֵ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן ... וְהָאַחֲר֖וֹן הִכְבִּ֑יד (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier) is mid-verse content the row leaves unused, and it is not a ruled onset class either. LEFT (the preceding unit's close, which the onset-only finding never weighed): וְהִנֵּ֨ה צָרָ֤ה וַחֲשֵׁכָה֙ מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה וַאֲפֵלָ֖ה מְנֻדָּֽח (oshb:Isa.8.22, byte tier) is a descriptive close — no refrain, no signature, no imperative, no formula — and the staged parashah inventory records no seg at Isa.8.22 or Isa.8.23 (nearest: SAMEKH at Isa.8.18 and SAMEKH at Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7; single witness, absence weighed as nothing); the preceding row's own rear-seam warrant is the same tonal reversal read from the other side. So the complete test finds NO ruled tier-1 signal on either side of MT 8:22|8:23 (= web:Isa.8.22|web:Isa.9.1): the finding is confirmed, not rescued. The seam's only byte-anchored relation binds the two verses as much as it turns them — the root-level antithesis of מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.8.22, byte tier) against מוּעָף֮ and מוּצָ֣ק (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier): form-distinct at skeleton tier (sweeps: the 8:22 gloom and anguish spellings stand at 1 and 2 verses, the 8:23 pair at 1 and 1; no two of the four share a skeleton), a lemma-level echo disclosed by neither row and not a ruled device. The nearest onset of the class the neighbouring rows accept as a driver — a fresh grammatical subject (web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7; web:Isa.11.1) — stands one verse INSIDE the row, הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ at oshb:Isa.9.1 (= web:Isa.9.2) (byte tier), which the row discloses and absorbs into its ki-chain argument; the second-person turn הִרְבִּ֣יתָ at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3) (byte tier; a K/Q verse, checked before slicing) is two verses in. The cut as placed coincides with the WEB chapter seam, while the MT chapter seam falls one verse later at that fresh-subject onset — tier-4 in both traditions, evidence for nothing, recorded only so that no repair leans on it. Severity: the prior adjudication ('defective front-seam warrant, not alone load-bearing') was already two-sided in substance — it checked the left for marks; the complete test adds that the left carries no ruled close and that the one cross-seam link is lemma-level continuity. Medium is confirmed rather than raised because the finding contests the warrant, not the placement (no respan filed; both adjacent rows cut here on the same ground), the row holds frontier_flag_considered true at medium and discloses the internal fresh-subject rival, and the remedy is proportionate — but only the confidence branch of the proposal survives the test that killed the original: re-arguing from the temporal-contrast pair would swap one non-ruled content signal for another, mid-verse and bound to the preceding verse by the gloom/anguish antithesis; medium_low is the honest band for a span whose front seam has no ruled warrant on either side and which carries the registered hazard stack at oshb:Isa.9.5-9.6 (= web:Isa.9.6-9.7): exegesis note at MT 9:5, K/Q plus SAMEKH at MT 9:6, K/Q at MT 9:2 (= web:Isa.9.3).

Rear seam web:Isa.10.34|web:Isa.11.1, both sides re-derived. THIS ROW'S OWN CLOSE: וְנִקַּ֛ף סִֽבְכֵ֥י הַיַּ֖עַר בַּבַּרְזֶ֑ל וְהַלְּבָנ֖וֹן בְּאַדִּ֥יר יִפּֽוֹל (oshb:Isa.10.34, byte tier, the whole verse) carries no ruled closing device — no refrain, no signature, no formula; the presentative הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת at oshb:Isa.10.33 (byte tier) is the internal seam candidate the row discloses — and the staged parashah inventory records SAMEKH at Isa.10.34 (single witness, tier-3; SAMEKH plus a K/Q note at Isa.10.32 inside the span). THE FOLLOWING UNIT'S ONSET: וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י opens oshb:Isa.11.1 verse-initially (byte tier) — an explicit scene shift with a fresh grammatical subject and figure (a shoot from Jesse's stump replacing the marching Assyrian and the felled Lebanon), the onset class the neighbouring rows themselves treat as the driver (web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7; web:Isa.11.1), waw-prefixed like the accepted formula onset וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא at oshb:Isa.7.18 (byte tier). The seam is therefore warranted from the right and corroborated at tier-3; the boundary is sound — as the finding itself says ('the following unit's tier-1 onset is never reached'). The finding was not onset-only in the defective sense: it names the right-side onset as the missing discriminator; the complete test confirms that the row's own close supplies nothing ruled and that the following onset is the seam's only tier-1 warrant. Verified from the shipped fields: the rationale's last sentence is descriptive ('the unit closes with the felled forest' plus the web:Isa.10.34 quotation), the rejected alternative treats only the internal web:Isa.10.33 candidate, device_notes' rear-edge datum is the tier-3 mark alone, and boundary_evidence_refs stops at web:Isa.10.34 — the following onset is absent from every field. One correction to the finding's colour, changing nothing: not every other row in this stretch names its following onset — the refrain-closed stanza at web:Isa.9.8-Isa.9.12 (= oshb:Isa.9.7-9.11) closes on the ruled refrain bracket instead — but a refrain close is a ruled warrant on the row's own side, which this row lacks. Medium confirmed: a rear seam left standing on a single-witness tier-3 mark in the row's fields while a byte-true tier-1 onset is available one verse on; repair as filed (add the oshb:Isa.11.1 onset as the rear-seam discriminator, add web:Isa.11.1 to boundary_evidence_refs), no span change.

Opening seam web:Isa.14.2|web:Isa.14.3, both sides re-derived. LEFT (the preceding unit's close): וְהָיוּ֙ שֹׁבִ֣ים לְשֹֽׁבֵיהֶ֔ם וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם (oshb:Isa.14.2, byte tier) is third-person narration to its last token — a 2nd-person suffix scan of oshb:Isa.14.1-14.2 returns 0 hits — with no ruled close device; the staged parashah inventory records SAMEKH at Isa.14.2 (single witness, tier-3). RIGHT (the row's own opening verse): וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.14.3, byte tier) is a verse-initial temporal-formula onset (skeleton class of the 'and it shall be in the day' opener: 14 verses book-wide, this the one non-'that day' member) that turns to direct second-person address inside the same clause — the scan of oshb:Isa.14.3 returns exactly four 2nd-person suffixes: the final token of וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔, both tokens of מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ, and the final token of אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד בָּֽךְ (all byte tier), against 0 in the two preceding verses. Two ruled tier-1 signals (formula onset, addressee shift) stand in the seam verse's own bytes: the seam is sound, and the finding says so. The defect is engagement, and it re-verifies field by field: boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.14.3 but no oshb:Isa.14.3; the rationale splices nothing from 14:3 and opens its Hebrew engagement at וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ (oshb:Isa.14.4, byte tier) — a 2ms verb, so the second-person frame IS byte-engaged one verse in, which is why this is engagement-class and not a missing warrant; device_notes and the signal key narrative_frame.direct_second_person_taunt rest the seam on 'the shift into direct second-person address at Isa.14.3' asserted from the WEB sentence alone; confidence ships high. Under the engagement standard (pointed splices plus tier labels mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim) a high-confidence row whose seam-verse warrant is engaged only in the translation is exactly the class the finding names. One further byte fact for the repair to disclose rather than fear: the rest-verb root recurs across this seam, וְהִנִּיחָ֖ם (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier) and הָנִ֤יחַ (oshb:Isa.14.3, byte tier), a skeleton-substring match (sweep: 4 verses skeleton) beside the eved-root echo the preceding row already discloses — root-level cross-seam cohesion that the addressee shift and formula onset outweigh, but which the cross-seam law asks to be named.
